title: A rapid test in a clinic
intro:
Illustrative data, made up for this book. In a clinic, 8 % of the patients tested have a certain infection. A rapid test has sensitivity 90 % and specificity 97 %. Let A = infected and B = the test is positive.

Give P(B), the share of tests that come back positive, and the positive predictive value P(A|B), each to four decimals.

In the Workbench: **Probability rules**, **What is known** *Likelihoods (Bayes)*, P(A) = 0.08, P(B|A) = 0.90, P(B|not A) = 1 − 0.97 = 0.03.

AGivenB.says: That is the sensitivity, P(B|A): the chance of a positive test if infected. The question asks the reverse, P(A|B): use Bayes' rule.

hints: P(B) = P(B|A)P(A) + P(B|not A)P(not A); P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A)/P(B) (item 3.4).
